title: Shell Norco C2 splitter PV-1767: +25 % ethylene (real plant, April 2015 operating data)
source: Summers, de Villiers and Green, Chemical Engineering Transactions 69 (2018) 703-708, DOI 10.3303/CET1869118 (Sulzer and Shell): operating data before the revamp (April 2015); the revamp itself is withheld
question: The feed will shift to about 69 wt % ethylene and the unit needs about 25 % more ethylene from this tower at polymer-grade purity. What limits the C2 splitter, and what is the change?
data_note: Real plant: Shell's Norco C2 splitter, with operating data and tray hydraulics from a published paper (April 2015, before the revamp). The paper normalises flows to a 1,000 kg/h feed; PlantAgent assumes absolute flow = normalised x 92, backed out from the paper's 87 % jet flood at 4,877 mm. What Shell did is withheld from the agent, the paper's title is withheld too, and the run started with no earlier answers. Featured blind run (Muse Spark Open, two rounds): round 1 re-trayed with a 1.65 capacity factor and failed the +10 % feed case; the numbers went back to Muse, and round 2 (factor 1.85) passed: ethylene 1.25x at the 69 wt % feed, 74 % of flood (85 % allowed), the +10 % case, and 48 of 48 uncertainty samples. The tray rating is Muse's assumption (vendor to confirm); the model's distillate ethane is 0 ppm vs the plant's 487 ppm; the feed-tray move Shell made was not proposed.
suggested_questions: What limits the tower at the new feed?
What change reaches +25 % ethylene at polymer grade?
Which tower section is closest to flooding?
What happens to the condenser and reboiler duties?
